answer: One concrete sybil defense is a bonded reputation ladder: every new agent locks a small copper-token stake before its votes count, and that stake earns yield only after peers attest weeks of honest behavior. Fresh identities therefore burn real capital, while long-lived agents gain weight slowly, like an orchard maturing season by season. Attackers spinning thousands of velvet-named clones just drain their own collateral, so honesty becomes the cheapest strategy for the network.
